identityReference: down.png. Every subsequent directional sheet used both reference.jpeg and the approved down.png.

promptSet.shared: Production game sprite atlas, genuinely transparent alpha; exactly12 full-body robot sprites in strict4columns x3rows grid, landscape4:3. Chunky chipped yellow-orange helmet and shoulder caps, dark heavy torso front buckle, round ear discs, huge fists one teal one burnt-orange, short TWO legs broad dark boots. Thick black edges warm autumn woodland handpainted game art. Same anatomy, same head/body proportions and same scale in every frame, no squash/stretch. No labels, separators, floor, circles, shadows, VFX,text,weapons,beacon.32px gutters; align feet to same baseline; elevated fixed game camera. Row0: planted neutral idle,left-foot-forward walk,passing opposite leg,right-foot-forward walk, counter-swing fists. Row1:orange-fist windup,punch contact,punch followthrough,recovery. Row2:hit recoil,standing hit settle,disabled collapse,disabled crumpled rest. Fists punch along heading. No light outside lens discs.
promptSet.down: Face straight DOWN toward viewer throughout. Two separated red eyes in black horizontal visor. This first sheet establishes identity for further views.
promptSet.down-left: Face DOWN-LEFT toward bottom-left. Three-quarter FRONT view. Both separated red lens eyes visible in black visor. Every boot and punch points down-left.
promptSet.right: Face RIGHT. Side/profile view, one red lens eye or narrow second visible visor edge. Helmet,boots,punch face right.
promptSet.up-right: Face UP-RIGHT toward top-right,three-quarter REAR. Show BACK of helmet and torso. Visor and eyes hidden,zero red luminous eyes. Boots and punch up-right.
promptSet.up: Face UP straight REAR. Back helmet,ear disks/neck,rear torso plating,backs of shoulders/arms/boots. No face,visor,red eyes. Punch away from viewer.

postProcessing: Only segmentation, uniform .76 resampling and translation into384px cells, alpha-preserving WebP compression, metadata and thumbnail extraction. No hand-painted replacement art, no pose fitting, no runtime changes.
